thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 Pager — kv-cache memory growth detected in prod-region-2.continuous-batching queue spike. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-frag (auto-attached metrics)
Sophie (oncall): seeing a rapid increase in `kv_cache.arena_used` across a subset of pods. OOMs on a few instances and degraded tail-latency for chat routes. Triage starting. @Rajiv @Maria pls ack.
Rajiv: ack. looking at instance logs now. initial hypothesis: continuous-batching growth combined with small-requests pattern -> slab fragmentation. PyTorch/CUDA malloc returning ENOMEM on a couple of allocs right after big sequences. stack traces show lots of small KV allocations.
Maria: copying metric snapshots — `kv_slots_used` jumped 3x ~09:12 UTC, fragmentation ratio up to 0.67. I see per-pod variance: ~20% of pods are hot. Likely allocator fragmentation, not immediate model mem leak. Also some 500s on /generate (latency spikes).
Sophie (oncall): impact: partial degradation of hosted customers in region-2 (small % of requests 5xx/timeout). No full cluster down. Support: @support-runner please collect customer list for region-2, mark any paid tenants with >SLA risk.
support-runner: collecting and DMing the list. No major enterprise customers impacted so far, a couple of startups on heavy chat workloads showing errors. :thinking_face:
Rajiv: repro logs snippet:
```
E 09:13:27 cuda malloc failed: out of memory, size=262144
W 09:13:27 kv_cache: slot_alloc failed, slab_free_count=2, arena_frag=0.68
I 09:13:27 batching: flush triggered, batch_size=128, queued=45
```
Rajiv: also saw `continuous_batch.max_tokens` set to 1024 on these nodes (custom config from previous perf tuning). That increases long-lived KV cache lifetime and exacerbates fragmentation.
Tim: quick mitigation suggestion: roll a config hotfix to reduce continuous_batch.max_tokens -> 256 for region-2 and enable kv_cache.slab_compaction=true (cheap background compaction). This should reduce long tails and let compaction free slabs.
Maria: agree. also propose enabling allocator arena tuning on the pod level: set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.6,arena_reserve:0.2` (example) — this will give CUDA allocator more aggressive release behavior. Need to be conservative.
Sophie (oncall): plan: 1) apply batching/config hotfix to 10% of region-2 (canary) 2) watch OOMs/fragmentation for 20m 3) if stable, ramp to 100% 4) run background compaction script on hot pods. @deploy-bot initiate canary patch now.
deploy-bot: Starting canary rollout: patching deployment `kv-worker` in prod-region-2 -> 10% (10 pods). Patch payload:
```
kubectl -n inference patch deployment kv-worker -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"kv-worker","env":[{"name":"CONTINUOUS_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS","value":"256"},{"name":"KV_SLAB_COMPACTION","value":"true"}]}]}}}}'
```
deploy-bot: Canary started — 10 pods patched. Will report health checks. :rocket:
Sophie (oncall): running a quick `kubectl exec` to tail OOM logs on the patched pods. Tim, can you pre-stage the compaction script? I don't want to run heavy compaction on all nodes at once.
Tim: compaction script ready — it'll run a bounded compaction per pod to avoid CPU spikes. Script:
```
#!/bin/bash
# run slab compaction loop, 3 passes max
for i in 1 2 3; do
  ./kv_cache_tool --compact --max-pages 1024 || break
  sleep 5
done
```
Tim: will run on the 10 canary pods now.
Maria: metrics update: after 6m into canary the patched pods show `kv_slots_used` down ~35% and fragmentation ratio down to 0.42. OOM count for patched pods -> 0 in last 6m. Non-patched pods still ramping.
Rajiv: good sign. I'm seeing reduced 500s from canary traffic. Suggesting ramp to 50%.
Sophie (oncall): ramping to 50% now. @deploy-bot proceed.
deploy-bot: Rolling to 50% (patching additional pods). Health checks continuing.
Sophie (oncall): Tim, start compaction on the remaining hot pods that aren't patched yet but limit concurrency to 3 at a time.
Tim: started compaction on 3 pods. CPU usage modest. No regressions.
Maria: at 20m after start, overall region trends: fragmentation median down 0.3, OOM event rate reduced by 88%. Tail latency improving. Customer errors dropping.
support-runner: notified affected customers of mitigation and ETA for full rollout. Most customers acknowledged. No escalations yet. :thumbsup:
Rajiv: root cause summary so far: previous perf tuning increased continuous batch size for throughput at the cost of longer KV lifetimes; combined with small-request patterns this led to inefficient packing of KV entries -> arena fragmentation -> cuda malloc pressure. The allocator didn't compact aggressively enough.
Sophie (oncall): next steps: 1) complete 100% rollout 2) schedule a follow-up to tune batch size per workload (profile) 3) create a patch to make `continuous_batch.max_tokens` default workload-aware and auto-cap when fragmentation rises 4) postmortem (include runbook updates)
deploy-bot: Rollout complete to 100% in prod-region-2. No failing pods. :white_check_mark:
Maria: leaving a note: we should add fragmentation alarms (frag_ratio > 0.5 on any pod triggers an alert) and add an automated compaction job when fragmentation persistent >5m.
Sophie (oncall): agreed. Also need an infra ticket to evaluate allocator heuristics (PyTorch/CUDA malloc behavior) and consider vendor recommendations. Rajiv/Maria can lead.
Zoe (next-oncall): taking handoff. Summary: P1 due to kv-cache fragmentation causing CUDA OOMs and increased 5xx in prod-region-2. Mitigation applied: lowered continuous_batch.max_tokens to 256 + enabled slab compaction; ran bounded compaction; patched to 100%. Observed metrics: fragmentation ratio improved (0.67 -> ~0.3), OOMs reduced 88%, tail latency improving. Customer impact: limited and notified. Actions in flight: add fragmentation alert, sched postmortem, evaluate allocator tunables.
Sophie (oncall): handover notes to @Zoe: 1) watch `kv_cache.fragmentation_ratio` and `cuda_malloc_errors` dashboards closely for 2 hours 2) escalate if either jumps >2x or any enterprise tenant reports sustained errors 3) request ops to run deeper leak scan if fragmentation recurs after compaction (ticket INFRA-alloc-2025). I'll be reachable for 30m.
Zoe (next-oncall): ack. I'll monitor and kick off postmortem doc. Thanks team. :pray:
incident-bot: Incident marked as mitigated by oncall at 09:58 UTC — monitoring continues. Record: mitigation: config-hotfix + bounded compaction + allocator tunables. Please file postmortem within 72h.
Sophie (oncall): closing thread on my side, leaving it open for postmortem updates. Great work everyone.
